parsed.explanation: Combined regime: no express criminalisation, but 'good morals' provisions (ss. 353-354) are documented as usable against public same-sex or gender-nonconforming conduct and are treated as de facto illegal, with no case law bounding reach. No legal gender recognition, and foreign-document treatment at entry is unsourced. No general SOGI anti-discrimination law (employment only), and no remedy for refused service or entry. Complaints go to police or the NHRC, but no outcomes are recorded. No official violence cases are cited, yet status and conduct are documented as taboo, with pervasive intolerance and fear of shunning. Documentation is thin and dated, so I extrapolate from the structural signals (open-ended morals enforcement, no recognition, no remedy) toward elevated risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign documents with amended markers are assessed against a framework with no domestic recognition equivalent; effect on entry or airport processing is unsourced.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy could feed into public-morals questioning if the visitor is visibly gender-nonconforming, but the sequence is not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Public same-sex or gender-nonconforming conduct can be prosecuted under ss. 353-354; no case law defines limits; no detention conditions for trans people are documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Police and NHRC complaint channel exists, with no recorded outcomes.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Open-ended morals provisions plus discretionary policing create a route from visibility to detention; no records show how it operates.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation documented; country-wide taboo and morals provisions apply uniformly on the record. Facility-access rules are not documented.

care_services.exposure: No care-access restriction for trans visitors is documented; no record of service denial remedies, and no general refusal-of-service remedy exists.
care_services.interaction: Refusals in health or other services would have no general legal remedy, so exposure could persist if discovered.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Good-morals provisions are the operative instrument for public conduct; public discussion of homosexuality is not tolerated; status is treated as taboo.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Employment-only discrimination protection; no SOGI prohibition in law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law and society align against visible non-conformity, so the state's morals provisions carry social licence.

minors_guardians.exposure: Family and community shunning on disclosure is documented; no minor-specific rule or custody exposure is recorded.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visitor travelling with a minor could face social or family-context exposure if discovered; the dossier does not document any child-specific mechanism.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A societal pattern of discrimination is recorded; no violence cases are cited and no trans-specific prevalence figure exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of documented incidents reflects thin documentation, not safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: LGBTI organisations cannot register; no legal gender recognition; no outcomes recorded for complaints; sources are dated or country-wide.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Police and NHRC complaint channel is documented but unevidenced in operation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin recourse combined with open-ended morals provisions leaves outcomes unbounded.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest analogue: police stops and detention of visitors with no imprisonment. This dossier documents no enforcement against trans people, so it is less exposed on the record, but the open-ended morals provisions and lack of any remedy keep it near 0.35.

Also has a morality provision with selective policing and undercover enforcement, which this dossier does not document. It is therefore rated higher, since no enforcement pattern or entrapment is recorded.
Has documented service and facility exclusion affecting residents and visitors. This dossier documents no comparable exclusion mechanism, so it is rated higher, though recourse is also thinner.

Has documented ejection and harassment of trans visitors with partial remedies. This dossier documents no visitor-facing harassment, so it is treated as less exposed on the record, but with weaker remedies.

parsed.synthesis: The operative exposure is the 'good morals' provisions, which are open-ended, undefined by case law and usable against public conduct, combined with documented taboo and intolerance and no general anti-discrimination remedy. No enforcement against trans people, no official violence, and no entry-document practice are documented, so the record is thin rather than reassuring. Structural signals (no recognition, no remedy, no recorded relief) are extrapolated toward elevated risk. The rating sits in the Elevated Risk band, below the 0.35 anchors that document enforcement.
